verdict.rationale: Sill's privacy page says there is no account and no server, so screen and keystrokes travel only between the user's own devices. The one documented outbound call, a daily update check to api.github.com, can be switched off with a setting. The docs never explicitly say there is no telemetry, analytics or crash reporting, so the opt-out covers only the update check and the rest of the story rests on implication. Missing for 10: an explicit no-telemetry/no-analytics statement, documentation of every outbound connection, and independent or hands-on verification that nothing else is sent.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can opt out of telemetry and usage tracking

citations.quote: Unless you turn off “Check for updates automatically” in Sill’s Settings › General, once a day it asks GitHub (api.github.com) whether a newer version of Sill has been released
There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices
Sill is free and open source.
